thread.title: S. Korea Joins List of Countries Investigating Apple for Slowing Down Phones - Investopedia (blog)

title: S. Korea Joins List of Countries Investigating Apple for Slowing Down Phones - Investopedia (blog)
text:
S. Korea Joins List of Countries Investigating Apple Slowing Down Phones By Daniel Liberto | Updated January 22, 2018 — 5:27 AM EST 
South Korea has become the latest country to investigate allegations that Apple Inc. ( AAPL ) deliberately slowed down older iPhones as part of a scam to convince customers to buy newer models. 
The Korea Herald reports that the Seoul Central District Prosecutors’ Office opened a probe with its intellectual property crime unit after a consumer group filed a complaint against Apple CEO Tim Cook and the head of the iPhone maker’s Korean unit. 
Seoul-based Citizens United for Consumer Sovereignty claimed that software updates designed to purposely slow down the performance of older iPhones are a scam aimed at boosting sales of new models. In its complaint, the consumer group asked that Apple be charged with fraud, property damage and obstruction of business by digital devices. 
South Korea isn’t the only country to open up an investigation into Apple’s practices. Italian, French, Chinese and U.S. authorities also recently launched probes into the company’s controversial software updates. Italian prosecutors are reportedly also investigating similar allegations made against Samsung Electronics Co Ltd. ( SSNLF ). 
Apple publicly admitted in December to intentionally slowing down iPhones after Reddit users and benchmarking firms produced evidence proving that older models quickly deteriorate over time. The tech giant insisted that it used software to reduce the performance levels of processors in order to prevent iPhones with aging batteries from shutting down. Older batteries, the company added, aren’t able to draw enough power during processor-intensive activities, leading to random crashes. 
That explanation wasn’t enough to prevent Apple from facing numerous lawsuits. Consumer groups in the U.S. and abroad claimed that the company’s actions were deceptive and not in the best interest of customers. (See also: Apple Sued After It Admitted It Slows Down Older Phones .) 
In response, Apple introduced new measures designed to make it easier for users to avoid future performance issues. The company offered discounts on battery replacements and then promised to let customers decide whether they want their iPhones to automatically slow down or not, courtesy of a new software update. (See also: Apple Will Allow Owners of Older Phones to Opt Out of Slow Down .)
